name: Merging antiphase twins
summary: Two spiders of the same colour with phases α and α+π and the same neighbourhood merge into one spider with phase 2α+π, with every connection doubled.
description:
Two spiders $u$ and $v$ are *antiphase twins* if they have the same colour, their phases differ by $\pi$, and they have the same neighbourhood: every other spider is connected to $u$ by as many wires as to $v$. Antiphase twins with phases $\alpha$ and $\alpha+\pi$ can be merged into a single spider with phase $2\alpha+\pi$ that is connected to each neighbour by twice as many wires.

Perdrix and Wang showed that, in the presence of the other rules, merging antiphase twins is equivalent to [supplementarity](../supplementarity/), which is the special case of twins of degree one sharing a single neighbour. This gives supplementarity a purely graphical meaning. The doubled wires can be removed in pairs with the [Hopf rule](../hopf/) when the neighbours have the opposite colour.
parameter_notes: n is the number of common neighbours of the twins (shown for n = 2, as X-spiders with one output each); holds for any common neighbourhood.
